topics.title: Selectors, Rules & the Cascade
topics.summary: Learn the basic grammar of CSS: choose elements with selectors, declare properties and values, and understand why one competing rule wins.

concepts.name: Rulesets
concepts.explanation: A ruleset combines a selector with a declaration block. Each declaration is a property/value pair such as color: white.

concepts.name: Selectors
concepts.explanation: Type, class, and id selectors target different sets of elements. Classes are the normal reusable styling hook; ids are unique document identifiers.

concepts.name: Cascade basics
concepts.explanation: When rules target the same property, origin, importance, specificity, and source order determine which declaration wins.

topics.challenge: Style the page background/text and create a reusable .card class with padding and a border.
topics.hint: Use one body rule and one class selector beginning with a dot.

topics.title: Color, Fonts & Text
topics.summary: Control readable typography using color, font families, sizes, weights, line height, alignment, and spacing.

concepts.name: Color values
concepts.explanation: CSS accepts named colors, hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl(), and newer color functions. Good contrast matters more than choosing a fashionable notation.

concepts.name: Font stack
concepts.explanation: font-family should normally include fallback fonts or a generic family such as sans-serif or monospace.

concepts.name: Readable text
concepts.explanation: font-size, line-height, letter-spacing, max-width, and spacing all affect readability. Avoid using tiny text or low contrast as decoration.

topics.challenge: Create readable body typography and give h1 a larger size and deliberate letter spacing.
topics.hint: Start with font-family and line-height on body so descendants inherit useful defaults.

topics.title: Box Model & Spacing
topics.summary: Reason about every element as content surrounded by padding, border, and margin, then control sizing predictably with box-sizing.

concepts.name: Four layers
concepts.explanation: Content is the inner box. Padding adds interior space, border surrounds padding, and margin creates space outside the border.

concepts.name: box-sizing
concepts.explanation: With border-box, declared width and height include padding and border. Many projects apply box-sizing: border-box globally for easier sizing.

concepts.name: Margin behavior
concepts.explanation: Vertical margins between normal block elements can collapse in some situations. Gap, padding, or layout systems can be clearer when you need explicit spacing.

topics.challenge: Create a .panel with width, padding, border and margin, and enable border-box sizing.
topics.hint: Remember that margin is outside the border while padding is inside it.

topics.title: Flexbox Fundamentals
topics.summary: Lay out items in one dimension and control direction, wrapping, alignment, flexible growth, and spacing.

concepts.name: Main and cross axes
concepts.explanation: flex-direction defines the main axis. justify-content distributes items along the main axis; align-items controls the cross axis.

concepts.name: Flexible sizing
concepts.explanation: flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis describe how an item participates when space is added or removed. The flex shorthand combines them.

concepts.name: Wrapping and gap
concepts.explanation: flex-wrap allows items to move to another line. gap creates consistent spacing without margin tricks.

topics.challenge: Create a flex row that spaces major groups apart and allows wrapping on smaller widths.
topics.hint: Set display:flex first, then think separately about main-axis and cross-axis alignment.

topics.title: Responsive Foundations
topics.summary: Build layouts that adapt to available space using fluid dimensions, media queries, and content-driven breakpoints.

concepts.name: Fluid first
concepts.explanation: Prefer flexible widths such as percentages, fr units, max-width, and min() before adding many media queries.

concepts.name: Media queries
concepts.explanation: @media conditionally applies rules based on features such as viewport width, input capability, motion preference, or color scheme.

concepts.name: Mobile-friendly sizing
concepts.explanation: The viewport meta tag belongs in HTML; CSS should then avoid fixed widths that force horizontal scrolling on narrow screens.

topics.challenge: Create a two-column layout that becomes one column below 700px.
topics.hint: Write the base layout first, then override only the property that must change inside @media.
